doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Growing up in Verona and Dry Jack
title: Seeing Return to Forever at Hamilton, 1973
summary: Lamb and Rowe recall hearing Chick Corea's Return to Forever, a spiritual experience that spurred Lamb's composing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: At Hamilton. That was like 1973 and that did the trick ‘cause there was a, you know these guys were brilliant. Stanley Clarke, Chick, Lenny White, Bill Connors was on guitar. And it was a spiritual experience. These guys were plugged in to the source. And I remember that chapel just like — and I was oh my God man, music can do that, you know lift you up. And it was a lot of improvisation. I remember there was a piano, a grand piano off the stage on the floor and Chick went down to start the second set, he climbed off the stage and went over and he did that. He improvised this thing and it was like, that’s the keys to the castle right there man.
I saw them about the same time.
And it was at Syracuse University. And I was in a band later that played Yes and all that stuff. But when I saw that group, with Bill Connors, it was the same thing. Like awestruck.

Yeah. It was awestruck you know. And we walked out of that, I remember Rich and I were like um hum, okay. And I don’t know why man, I was composing pretty quickly when I started playing piano, which I was about fifteen. And as soon as that happened the composition thing really took off.
